Indian Standard
GRADING FOR LINSEED FOR OIL MILLING

o.

FOR E W 0 R D

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 8 May 1968, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseed. Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.1 The linseed plant Linum usitattsstmum is cultivated either for seed or the fibre. In India the plant is cultivated only for its seed which yields an oil used mainly for industrial purposes, namely, in the manufacture of varnishes, paints, linoleum, enamels, oil cloth, printing inks. The oil is also used in veterinary medicines and for edible purposes in some parts of the country.

0.3 Indian linseed is broadly classified as bold and small. The oil
content is more in bold linseed as compared to small seeds. of two colours, brown and yellow. They are

0.3.1 Bold linseed is principally grown in Rajasthan, South-West Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.

0.3.1 Small linseed is grown in eastern and northern parts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, eastern Madhya Pradesh, Orissa and West Bengal.
0.4 The specification for the oil obtained from the linseed is covered by IS : 7S~1967�.
0.5 This standard contains clause 5.1 which calls for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis. shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained J~. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
~-

�Speoifloation fOl' Iinaeed oil, raw and refined (reviled). tRulea for roundinK otT numerical values ( reV/led ).

IS : 4617 � 1968
1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of grading and the requirements for linseed for oil milling, along with the relevant methods of sampling and test.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of this standard, definitions given under Z of

IS: 3S79�1966* shall apply.
3. GRADES

3.1 The material shall be of six grades, namely, Bold Grade 1, Bold Grade 2, Bold Grade 3, Small Grade 1, Small Grade 2 and Small q,ade 3. 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The material shall be obtained from the plant Linum us/tat/sstmum Linn., belonging to family Linaceace.

4.2 Bold linseed shall not weigh more than 135 seeds per gram. 4.3 Small linseed shall not weigh more than 170 seeds per gram.
4.4 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1.

4.5 The material shall also be free from argemone and castor seeds.

5. PAC"ING
5.1 The material shall be supplied in clean, dry, sound, single, new or unmended BeTwill bags in merchantable condition as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

6. MARKING

6.1 The bags shall be marked with the name, grade and weight of the
linseed, the year of the crop and the source of supply.

7. S.utPLING 7.1 Representative samples for the purpose of the tests shall be drawn
as prescribed in IS : 41IS-1967t.

8. TESTS
8.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in IS : 3579..1966*.
